prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 that enabled a new class of therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots rank B046 first, but agreement alone is not the argument. The discovery arc is unusually complete: proglucagon processing, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, its glucose-dependent insulinotropic action, and central and gastric effects. These findings were then converted into drugs whose benefit in diabetes, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes has been confirmed in large independent trials. The mechanism is decades old and replicated, so maturity is not in doubt. The three-person trio of Holst (physiology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and translational proof of concept) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) maps onto the physiological discovery rather than the industrial optimisation that followed.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the weak point. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others is contested, and Habener is not among the credited names. Leaving out Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose long-acting analogue design made the drugs clinically practical, could be read as rewarding the physiology while excluding the step that created the medicine. A three-person cap forces a choice between a physiology prize and a physiology-plus-drug-development prize. If the committee thinks the drug-development step is itself the discovery, the configuration is incomplete.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks B015 third with Hall and Schreiber, preferring a leaner pair and treating Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work as less necessary.
responses.response: I disagree on the allocation. Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast, but the mammalian mTORC1/2 architecture and nutrient-sensing mechanisms (raptor, rictor, the amino-acid sensing pathway) came mainly from Sabatini's group. That work is what connects TOR to human physiology and disease. Schreiber's FKBP12-rapamycin chemistry is important, but it describes drug binding more than growth-control biology. I would put Sabatini ahead of Schreiber, and in any case I would keep B015 as an alternative to the trio on B046, not above it.

responses.point: Svenningsson places B031 (UPR; Mori and Walter) second, as a clean two-person configuration of a mature, textbook discovery with relevance to neurodegeneration.
responses.response: I agree that B031 is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and that the basic discovery is mature. I rank it fourth because translation into medicine is still emerging, and the allocation is not fully closed: Ron, Kaufman and Sidrauski-type work on PERK, ATF6 and the integrated stress response sits outside the credited pair. I would support B031 as a second part if the committee wants a basic-science component. I do not think it displaces B046 as the lead, since the prize is meant to favour discoveries with demonstrated benefit to humankind, and B046 shows that benefit at scale.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B040 second and B049 third, and credits CAR-T to June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, with Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work forming a legitimate third pillar.
responses.response: I take the point that Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials are a real conceptual foundation. I still think the decisive CAR design contributions are Sadelain's costimulated 19-28z constructs and June's clinical translation with 4-1BB, so a June and Sadelain pair is the more defensible attribution. If the committee wants Rosenberg, I would want the citation to state clearly that it is for adoptive cell therapy and engineered T cells. The ranking differences between us on B040 are small. We differ more on whether to credit a third person at all than on the merit of the field.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks B044 (Feldmann and Maini, TNF blockade) fourth, describing it as mature and arguably overdue, while saying she tries not to let her clinical familiarity inflate her view.
responses.response: The TNF case is strong: a clear concept-to-clinic story with decades of confirmation. My reservation is attribution. TNF blockade rests on a larger group than the two credited names, including TNF cloning and cachectin work and the antibody and fusion-protein engineers. That makes the credit harder to defend than for B046. I did not rank B044 in my top eight, so I accept that her view and mine differ. I would be interested in how she would resolve the credit allocation. I am not convinced it is as clean as the two-person framing suggests.

responses.point: El Manira ranks optogenetics (B049) second, favouring Deisseroth with the channelrhodopsin discoverers Nagel and Hegemann and leaving out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck.
responses.response: I rank B049 seventh, lower than he does. The method is transformative and well replicated. My difficulty is that it is mainly a research tool, with clinical translation still early. The attribution among six credible claimants (Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck and the three he names) is also hard to resolve fairly within three names. A tool prize has precedent, and I do not dismiss it. Still, I would sooner see the committee settle the attribution questions on B046 and B040 before spending a slot on a field where any three-person choice will look arbitrary to someone.

uncertainties: Whether Knudsen should be included in place of Mojsov or Drucker if the committee treats long-acting analogue development as part of the core discovery.
How much weight the committee should give to the contested early GLP-1 priority record (Mojsov versus Habener) when settling the final three names.
Whether to pair B046 with a second distinct achievement. The three-person cap means a second part would require reducing the B046 trio.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B046 or the alternatives. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén, but neither is a credited candidate on the shortlist. My own field of single-cell methods and RNA processing is not directly represented among the shortlisted discoveries, though B024 (sequencing) is a related technology that I ranked third in my opening ballot and am not proposing here.
